activities.description: Discusses the growth of powerlifting in recent years.
Mentions various drug-tested and non-drug-tested powerlifting federations.
Talks about impressive lifts he's seen in the USAPL Raw Nationals.
Compares and contrasts drug-tested and non-drug-tested records.
Mentions Powerlifting Watch as a source for information and records.
Cautions viewers about potential inaccuracies in the records.
Provides specific examples of records in different weight classes.
Discusses the weight class differences between federations.
Highlights Ray Williams' record as the biggest total ever in super heavyweight.
Emphasizes that the point is not to discuss steroids.
Points out that most records are recent, indicating fast growth.
Notes the increasing number of impressive lifts in the drug-tested category.
Analyzes factors contributing to the narrowing gap between drug-tested and non-drug-tested records.
Comments on the rising popularity of powerlifting among women.
Attributes growth to better information and programming availability.
Suggests that improved programming leads to faster progress and longer participation in the sport.
Mentions Bryce Lewis as an example of consistent training leading to success.
Acknowledges the role of drugs in strength sports.
Refers to the documentary Icarus, highlighting drug use in professional sports.
Notes the significant difference in body mass between natural and non-natural pro bodybuilders.
Observes a smaller discrepancy in the strength world.
States he's not a steroid expert.
Reiterates the observation that drug-tested and non-drug-tested records are converging.
Discusses the complexities of drug testing in powerlifting.
Mentions critiques of drug testing stringency in the IPF and USAPL.
Points out other factors influencing records, like equipment differences.
Summarizes that there's no clear answer to the questions raised.
Concludes the discussion, highlighting the camaraderie in the powerlifting community.
Asks viewers to like the video if they enjoyed it.
